strawberry.store: Unwashed, at room temperature, and eat the same day if you can.
strawberry.preserve: Strawberry jam, or freeze for smoothies.
strawberry.use: Warm from the plant, or with cream.

raspberry.store: Unwashed in the fridge for a day or two.
raspberry.preserve: Freeze on a tray, then bag; or make jam.
raspberry.use: With yoghurt, in a crumble, or by the handful.

blackberry.store: In the fridge for a day or two.
blackberry.preserve: Freeze on a tray; bramble jelly.

blackcurrant.store: On the strig in the fridge for a few days.
blackcurrant.preserve: Freeze whole, or make jam or cordial.

redcurrant.store: On the strig in the fridge for a few days.
redcurrant.use: Jelly with lamb, or a summer pudding.

gooseberry.store: In the fridge for a week or two.

blueberry.store: In the fridge for a week.
blueberry.preserve: Freeze on a tray, then bag.
blueberry.use: On porridge, in muffins, or by the handful.

rhubarb.store: Stems in the fridge for a week; the leaves are poisonous, so compost them.
rhubarb.preserve: Chop and freeze raw, or rhubarb and ginger jam.
rhubarb.use: Crumble, compote, or roasted with orange.

apple.store: Wrap the unblemished ones singly and keep somewhere cool and dark for months.
apple.preserve: Stew and freeze, dry in rings, or make chutney.
apple.use: Eating apples raw; cookers baked, stewed or in a crumble.

pear.store: Pick hard, then ripen at room temperature: a pear is ripe for about a day.
pear.preserve: Poach and freeze, or spiced pickled pears.
pear.use: Ripe with cheese, or poached in wine.

plum.store: At room temperature for a few days.
plum.preserve: Plum jam, or halve, stone and freeze.
plum.use: Raw when ripe, or roasted with honey.

cherry.store: In the fridge for a few days.
cherry.preserve: Stone and freeze, or cherry jam.
cherry.use: From the bowl, or a clafoutis.

fig.store: Eat them the day you pick them.
fig.preserve: Fig jam, or dry in a low oven.
fig.use: Torn open with ham and honey.

grape-vine.store: In the fridge for a week.
grape-vine.preserve: Freeze for snacks, or make jelly.
grape-vine.use: From the bunch, or roasted with sausages.

quince.store: Somewhere cool, away from other fruit: they scent everything.
quince.use: Slow-poached until pink, with cheese or in a tart.

medlar.store: Leave them to soften (blet) on a tray for a few weeks.
medlar.use: The soft flesh scooped out with cream, or jelly with cheese.

damson.store: In the fridge for a few days.
damson.use: Too sharp to eat raw: jam, crumble or gin.

greengage.store: At room temperature for a day or two.
greengage.use: The sweetest plum, eaten ripe from the tree.

apricot.store: At room temperature until ripe, then the fridge.
apricot.preserve: Apricot jam, or halve, stone and freeze.

peach.preserve: Poach and freeze, or make jam.
peach.use: Ripe over the sink, or grilled with mascarpone.

mulberry.store: Eat straight away: they barely keep.
mulberry.use: From the tree, with stained fingers.

morello-cherry.store: In the fridge for a few days.
morello-cherry.preserve: Morello cherry jam, or freeze for pies.
morello-cherry.use: Too sour to eat raw: pies, jam, and Black Forest gateau.

tayberry.store: In the fridge for a day or two.

jostaberry.store: In the fridge for a few days.

whitecurrant.store: On the strig in the fridge for a few days.
whitecurrant.use: Sweeter than red: on yoghurt, or in jelly.

honeyberry.store: In the fridge for a few days.
honeyberry.use: Like blueberries, with a sharp edge.

hardy-kiwi.store: Ripen at room temperature, then the fridge for weeks.
hardy-kiwi.use: Eaten whole, skin and all, like grapes.

cape-gooseberry.store: In their husks at room temperature for weeks.

japanese-wineberry.store: In the fridge for two or three days.
japanese-wineberry.preserve: Freeze on a tray, or make jam.
japanese-wineberry.use: Fresh with cream, or in a summer pudding.

loganberry.store: In the fridge for a day or two.
loganberry.preserve: Freeze on a tray, or make jam.
loganberry.use: Sharp: best cooked, in crumbles and jam.

boysenberry.store: In the fridge for a day or two.
boysenberry.preserve: Freeze on a tray, or make jam.
boysenberry.use: Fresh, or in pies and jam.

cranberry.use: Sauce for turkey; dried in muffins.

lingonberry.store: In the fridge for a week or two.

bilberry.store: In the fridge for a few days.
bilberry.preserve: Freeze on a tray, or make jam.
bilberry.use: In tarts and muffins: stronger than blueberries.

elderberry.store: Flowers used the day they’re picked; berries in the fridge for a day.
elderberry.preserve: Elderflower cordial; berries frozen or made into jelly.
elderberry.use: Elderflower cordial and fritters; berries in crumbles and jelly, always cooked.

sea-buckthorn.store: Frozen on the sprig for months.
sea-buckthorn.use: Sharp, tropical juice: in cordials, sorbets and with sugar.

goji.store: In the fridge for a few days.
goji.preserve: Dry them, spread on a tray.
goji.use: Dried in muesli, or fresh in a fruit salad.

aronia.store: In the fridge for a week.
aronia.preserve: Freeze, or make jam with apple.
aronia.use: Too sharp to eat raw: cooked with apple, in juice or jam.

serviceberry.store: In the fridge for a few days.
serviceberry.use: Fresh, a little like blueberry and almond, or in muffins.

chilean-guava.store: In the fridge for a few days.
chilean-guava.use: Eaten from the bush, or in muffins.

worcesterberry.store: In the fridge for a few days.
worcesterberry.use: In pies and fools, like gooseberry.

cornelian-cherry.store: In the fridge for a few days.
cornelian-cherry.use: Sharp: jam, or a syrup for drinks.

hazelnut.store: In their shells somewhere dry for months.
hazelnut.use: Fresh and milky in September; roasted in winter.

walnut.store: Dried in the shell for months.
walnut.preserve: Dry in the shell; pickle green ones in June.
walnut.use: In cakes, salads and bread; pickled with cheese.

sweet-chestnut.store: In the fridge for a couple of weeks.
sweet-chestnut.use: Roasted, or in stuffing and soups.

almond.store: Dried in the shell for months.
almond.use: Fresh green almonds, or roasted and salted.

cherry-plum.store: In the fridge for a few days.

sloe.preserve: Freeze, then steep in gin with sugar.
sloe.use: Sloe gin, or sloe jelly with apple.

crab-apple.store: Somewhere cool for a few weeks.
crab-apple.use: Jelly, with lamb or on toast; a few in apple pie.

asian-pear.use: Raw and cold, or sliced into salads.

persimmon.store: At room temperature until soft as jelly.
persimmon.use: Spooned from the skin, or in cakes.

olive.store: Cured olives keep for months in brine.
olive.preserve: Cure in brine for weeks before eating.
olive.use: Cured, then with bread and oil.

lemon.store: At room temperature for a week, in the fridge for a month.
lemon.preserve: Freeze the zest and juice; preserve in salt.
lemon.use: Everything: zest, juice, curd and preserved lemons.

kumquat.store: In the fridge for a few weeks.
kumquat.use: Whole, sliced into salads, or as marmalade.

kiwi.store: Firm ones in the fridge for weeks; ripen at room temperature.
kiwi.use: Halved and spooned, or in fruit salad.

passion-fruit.store: At room temperature for a week.
passion-fruit.use: Spooned over yoghurt, pavlova and ice cream.

pomegranate.store: Whole in the fridge for weeks.
pomegranate.use: Seeds over salads, rice and yoghurt.

loquat.store: In the fridge for a few days.
loquat.preserve: Poach in syrup, or make jam.

feijoa.store: At room temperature until soft, then the fridge.
feijoa.preserve: Freeze the pulp, or make chutney.
feijoa.use: Halved and spooned, or in crumble.

pawpaw.store: In the fridge for a couple of days.
pawpaw.use: Spooned out like custard; in ice cream.

akebia.store: At room temperature for a day or two.
akebia.use: The sweet pulp spooned out, seeds spat.

schisandra.store: Dried berries in a jar for a year.
schisandra.use: Steeped in water for a sharp, five-flavoured drink.

salal.store: In the fridge for a few days.
salal.use: In jam, or dried like raisins.

strawberry-tree.store: In the fridge for a day or two.
strawberry-tree.use: Mild and grainy: best in jam.

rowan.store: In the fridge for a few days.
rowan.use: Cooked only: bitter jelly for game and lamb.

mirabelle.store: In the fridge for a few days.
mirabelle.use: Fresh, or in tarts and jam.

black-raspberry.store: In the fridge for a day or two.
black-raspberry.preserve: Freeze on a tray, or make jam.
black-raspberry.use: Fresh, or in jam: rich and sweet.

white-mulberry.store: In the fridge for a day.

service-tree.store: Spread out somewhere cool until soft.
service-tree.use: Eaten when bletted, or in jelly.

autumn-olive.store: In the fridge for a few days.
autumn-olive.preserve: Make into a fruit leather or jam.

goumi.store: In the fridge for a few days.
goumi.use: Fresh when fully ripe, or in jam.

chinese-dogwood.store: In the fridge for a day.
chinese-dogwood.use: Sweet custardy pulp, spooned from the skin.

ground-cherry.store: In their husks at room temperature for weeks.
ground-cherry.use: Fresh from the husk, in jam or on cakes.

musk-strawberry.store: In the fridge for a day.
musk-strawberry.preserve: Freeze, or make a tiny pot of jam.
musk-strawberry.use: Fresh, a few at a time, with cream.

evergreen-huckleberry.store: In the fridge for a few days.

japanese-quince.store: Somewhere cool for weeks: they scent a room.
japanese-quince.use: Cooked only: jelly, or a little in apple pie.

tamarillo.store: At room temperature until soft, then the fridge.
tamarillo.use: Scooped out with sugar, or in chutney.

filbert.store: In their shells somewhere dry for months.
filbert.use: Fresh or roasted; ground into cakes.
